title: ‘If the bot gets it wrong, who’s liable?’ Retailers enter the unknown with AI shopping assistants on Black Friday
summary: Brands know use of agents such as Meta Muse is on the rise but are unlikely to hand them the keys to the shop Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to? They promise to find the best Black Friday deals, source Christmas gifts and find the ingredients for a romantic dinner. This week’s UK launch of the Muse AI assistant by the owner of Facebook and Instagram promises to transform how we shop – and how retailers make money. Continue reading...

title: Water firms to identify 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts
summary: Department for Work and Pensions to provide data about households missing out on WaterSure support scheme Water companies will use government data to identify as many as 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts, after criticism that not enough people are aware of the £428 support for their annual bills. The Department for Work and Pensions will provide information to identify and contact a quarter of a million households who are missing out on support to which they are entitled under the WaterSure scheme . title: Labour’s split over Rosebank oilfield exposed by letter from nearly 100 MPs
summary: Exclusive: Frontbenchers join scores of party colleagues urging Burnham not to let ministers approve project Opinion: Why Labour MPs are opposing Rosebank Podcast: are resignations next? Labour’s internal divisions over the giant Rosebank oilfield have spilled into the open, with nearly 100 Labour MPs – including a handful of frontbenchers – writing to the prime minister to express their opposition to the project. Ninety-two backbenchers and at least four frontbenchers have signed a letter to Andy Burnham urging him not to let his ministers approve the scheme for the biggest undeveloped field in UK waters. title: Up to 1.4m UK workers risk missing out on zero-hours shake-up, say unions
summary: Andy Burnham is warned against calls from bosses to water down employment rights legislation Andy Burnham is being warned that 1.4 million workers will be at risk of being stuck in insecure jobs if a forthcoming ban on zero-hours contracts is watered down. The prime minister is under pressure from business leaders to scale back last year’s Employment Rights Act, which is being introduced in stages over 2026 and 2027. Continue reading...
